competitive_position.basis: Stated in the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Demand is volatile and sensitive to U.S. elections, crime fears, and perceived gun-control risk, with unified Republican federal control cited as negatively impacting recent demand.
quotes: For example, we believe demand for our products was negatively impacted in recent years by unified Republican control of the executive and legislative branches of the federal government as a result of a perceived lower risk of federal gun control legislation and regulation.

As a result of these significant fluctuations in demand, our operating results can vary significantly from period to period, and we may build and maintain inventory levels that are significantly in excess of customer demand.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Federal ATF oversight, state product and magazine bans, excise taxes, and state handgun rosters threaten product eligibility and market access.
quotes: If we fail to comply with ATF rules and regulations, the ATF may limit our activities or growth, fine us, or, ultimately, put us out of business.

For example, certain states (i) prohibit the sale of modern sporting rifles; (ii) restrict magazine capacity; (iii) have raised the minimum age for buying firearms; or (iv) levy excise taxes on firearm, firearm component, and ammunition sales.
Certain of our products have been removed from the California roster in the past (meaning that they can no longer lawfully be sold by retailers) and may be removed in the future.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Active enforcement of state firearm industry accountability laws—including one lawsuit naming the company as a defendant—and potential weakening of the PLCAA expose Smith & Wesson to civil litigation risk.
quotes: Certain states have also adopted so called "gun industry accountability" or "firearm industry responsibility" laws that attempt to facilitate the filing of civil lawsuits by the respective state government or private individuals against firearm industry participants.
These statutes are being actively enforced, and we are a defendant in one such action.

If the PLCAA (or state law equivalents of the PLCAA) were repealed, amended, or reinterpreted, firearm manufacturers could face a significant increase in litigation, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, operating results, and financial condition.

For example, Canada has banned the sale, purchase, or transfer of various firearms within Canada, subject to certain exceptions.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A.
